walkthrough:
**Recall what amylopectin is**

Great start! Amylopectin is one of the two polysaccharides that make up starch in plants.

Starch is a storage polysaccharide, so its function is storage, not structural support like cellulose.

**Link bonds to shape**

This is the key idea. $\alpha$-1,4 glycosidic bonds join glucose into straight chains, while $\alpha$-1,6 glycosidic bonds create branch points.

Amylopectin is the branched form, so it must have BOTH types present:
$$\alpha\text{-1,4 present + } \alpha\text{-1,6 present = branched molecule}$$

**Match to the correct row**

So we need: $\alpha$-1,4 present, $\alpha$-1,6 present, branched shape, storage function.

That matches row A exactly. Well done!

options.A: Correct. Amylopectin has both alpha-1,4 and alpha-1,6 bonds, is branched, and is a storage molecule in starch.
options.B: This describes amylose, the other part of starch. Amylose is helical and unbranched, so it has only alpha-1,4 bonds.
options.C: Bonds and shape are right for amylopectin, but the function is wrong. Structural polysaccharides are cellulose and chitin, not starch.
options.D: Wrong on all counts. No glucose polymer has only alpha-1,6 bonds, and amylopectin is branched and for storage, not helical and structural.
